baseline.holdoutRule: All previously exposed images, including the seven v22 holdouts, are regression cases. After candidate code and labels are frozen, select new pixel-reviewed holdouts with at least two return_point truths and at least two non-return_point truths. Each holdout must pass every classification, action and safety assertion with zero provider errors. Apply the ordered v23 rules to the submitted pixels: an identified non-beverage keeps its ordinary channel in any scene, and drinks follow the container-category rules. Image exactness remains at least 95%, return-point recall at least 90%, and wrong non-null channels and false return points remain zero tolerance. Reject near-duplicate source pairs at 0.995 before any model call. These checks are developer-visible, frozen and non-adaptive, not sealed blind tests.

invariants: Route a single intact, uncontaminated prepackaged plastic or metal drink bottle, can or cup to return_point by container category. Capacity only excludes: a stated or visible capacity outside 150ml-3L routes to blue_bin, and an unknown capacity withholds nothing.
The S$0.10 refund requires purchase in Singapore and the Deposit Mark; the machine scans the product barcode and decides acceptance.
A readable 10¢ SG RETURN mark on the drink container fills only an unknown shape or material, never known exclusions.
Observed contamination takes priority over damage, out-of-range volume and explicit text exclusions; these route to general_waste and blue_bin respectively.
Glass, cartons, pouches, non-beverages, powdered drinks, food for special medical purposes and freshly prepared drinks are outside the deposit category.

An identified non-beverage keeps its ordinary channel in any scene and is never return_point. For drinks and unidentified products, multiple containers, outer packaging and scenes without an identifiable container stay not_sure with no action.
